5.subject: One warm parchment blueprint forms a compact amber disk beneath a single dark-steel drafting compass, whose two legs frame one simple arc-blue gear outline. The sheet, compass, and one blue line read together as a bold centered emblem rather than a busy workbench scene.
5.perspective: Straight overhead macro view with the blueprint-and-compass emblem centered inside an imagined circular socket, all detail inside the middle 55%, and all four corners empty.
5.background: A deep cool-charcoal field with only hazy iron texture far behind it, separating the warm amber parchment, dark compass, and bright arc-blue line.
5.notes: Hero power art must read at icon size. No table, loose components, extra gears, tools, readable labels, numerals, hands, finished construct, or detail outside the central circle.

6.subject: One round disk of shadow-black sealing wax bears a broad blade-silver crescent impression and one toxic-lime pinprick at its center, with a thin midnight-purple smoke halo hugging the rim. The high-contrast seal reads as one physical icon with a clean circular silhouette.
6.perspective: Straight overhead macro view with the complete wax seal centered inside an imagined circular socket, all detail inside the middle 55%, and all four corners empty.
6.background: A warm amber-brown leather field with soft golden haze, providing strong temperature and value contrast behind the black wax and cold silver.
6.notes: Hero power art must read at icon size. No glove, letters, runes, target reticle, skull icon, blood, victim, readable contract, UI symbol, or detail outside the central circle.

7.subject: One compact crescent wall built from three interlocking cool-grey granite slabs rises from a narrow base, its iron-black feet wedged together and two pale-quartz seams glowing where the stones lock. One rusted-bronze brace makes the single barrier feel old, repaired, and immovable.
7.perspective: Low frontal three-quarter icon view with the complete crescent barrier centered inside an imagined circular socket, all detail inside the middle 55%, and all four corners empty.
7.background: A warm ember-orange dusk over a softly blurred ruined road, separating the cool grey stone wall from the horizon.
7.notes: Hero power art must read at icon size. No defender, castle, giant cliff, explosive eruption, carved writing, projectile, or detail outside the central circle; this is one local protective wall.

8.subject: One palm-sized storm-silver double-ring conductor holds a bright cyan spark across its open center, leaving one sharp gold-white zigzag between the joined rings. The compact device and spark read together as one controlled circular emblem, not a full lightning storm.
8.perspective: Straight-on macro icon view with the complete double-ring conductor centered inside an imagined circular socket, all detail inside the middle 55%, and all four corners empty.
8.background: A deep charcoal field with soft hazy violet-grey vapor, maximizing value contrast around the storm-silver rings and cyan-gold spark.
8.notes: Hero power art must read at icon size. No caster, enemy figures, labels, giant bolt, explosion, extra rings, or detail outside the central circle.

51.subject: A footman's thrusting lance seen from the side: a long narrow leaf-shaped blade of dark char-black iron, fine ember-red cracks glowing faintly along its spine, socketed into a collar of scorched bronze on a charred wooden shaft. The blade and collar sit high in the frame and read large and unmistakably as a LANCE head, while the shaft runs down out of the bottom of the picture. A few small gold sparks drift up out of the cracks. Plain, cheap, well-used field gear rather than a treasure — but a full-sized weapon, not a knife.
51.perspective: Set WELL BACK and shot with a long lens — near-orthographic, minimal perspective falloff, the lance presented close to its true side profile with NO foreshortening. The head is held high and roughly upright, filling most of the circle's height, and the charred shaft descends from it and runs CLEAN OFF THE BOTTOM EDGE of the frame so the eye reads the weapon as continuing past the picture. Only that one end is cropped; the head is whole and unclipped.
51.background: A cold, dim blue-grey field with faint cool haze, no setting and no ground, opposing the char-black and ember-red of the lance.
51.notes: Weapon art renders into a CIRCULAR SOCKET, so keep everything that matters inside the middle 60% and never lay the weapon corner to corner — but do not achieve that by tipping it at the camera. Either the whole weapon is in frame or the shaft exits the frame edge; a shaft that stops in mid-air is not acceptable. The head must be large and clearly a LANCE head, not a dagger. This must NOT resemble Scorch Blade (ember_scorch_blade): that one is a broad molten cleaver throwing sparks; this is a slim, mostly-dark lance head with only thin ember cracks. It is a 1-mana common — plain, worn field gear rather than a hero's weapon, but plain in ornament, not small in size. The object alone — no hand, no wielder, no ground, no scene. PLACEMENT: this row is setId CORE, so candidates land under art-pipeline/card-art/CORE/, but the FINAL art ships to Assets/Art/Cards/EMBERFALL/ember_cinder_lance.png — Assets/Art/Cards/CORE/ holds hero powers only.

1059.subject: A palm-sized Gear Wisp formed from three mismatched brass cogs orbiting a bright arc-blue core, with two tiny copper stabilizer fins and a loose coil spring trailing like a tail. It hovers with a slight mechanical wobble, newly assembled and useful rather than cute or animal-like.
1059.perspective: Close eye-level three-quarter portrait with the entire small wisp centered and loose negative space around its clean circular silhouette.
1059.background: A dark oiled-steel parts drawer and cool slate workshop wall, softly blurred so the warm brass and arc-blue core read at mobile size.
1059.notes: Keep it visibly smaller and simpler than Assembly Drone: no limbs, face, swarm, tools, text, or large machinery.

1060.subject: A knee-high wedge of dark granite stands upright on two broad rubble feet, its front face naturally split into a shield-like plane with one pale-quartz eye glowing from a narrow crack. A rusted-bronze staple binds a broken corner and a tuft of moss grows from the rear seam.
1060.perspective: Close low eye-level portrait with the entire small shard construct, both feet, and repaired corner clearly contained in the central frame.
1060.background: A warm lantern-lit mason's yard of ochre dust and blurred timber braces, opposing the shard's cool iron-grey mass.
1060.notes: Bulwark reads through the broad planted wedge. Keep it smaller and more primitive than Pebble Sentinel, with no arms, weapon, mouth, or giant scale.
